# BBC SPORT | Football | My Club | Preston | Sunderland withdraw Nugent offer
E-mail this to a friend Printable version Sunderland withdraw Nugent offer  Nugent joined Preston from Bury in January 2005 **Sunderland have pulled out of the race for Preston striker David Nugent.** According to the Black Cats website, they agreed a fee believed to be £7m with the North End for the 22-year-old but will now focus on other targets. Club chief executive Peter Walker said: "I can confirm we have withdrawn our offer for the player. "Naturally work continues behind the scenes to strengthen our squad ahead of the new season and talks are on-going with a number of targets." Nugent was given permission to speak to two clubs after he returned from duty with the England Under-21 squad at the European Championship last month. One of the teams was believed to be Sunderland, while West Ham and Everton were also linked with him. BBC Sport understands that talks had taken place with the player and his representatives for a month before Sunderland boss Roy Keane became frustrated with the situation. 606: DEBATE Your views on Nugent's future Nugent joined Preston from Bury in January 2005 for a fee believed to be in the region of £100,000. The Liverpool-born forward has made 94 Championship appearances for Preston, scoring 33 goals. Sheffield United tried to buy him in the January 2007 transfer window but North End rejected the offer. But the striker made it clear last season that he saw his future in the Premiership. "I want to be playing in the Premiership week in, week out, that's where I need to be," he said. "I want it to be with Preston, but if not, it'll have to be somewhere else." Preston finished seventh in last season's Championship, missing out on a place in the play-offs. Nugent is an Everton fan and has previously said: "My hero was Duncan Ferguson and, hopefully, I will play for them in my career and I'm confident I will do." He made his full England debut in the win over Andorra in March, scoring in the final minute of the game. The cap was the first by a Preston player since Sir Tom Finney and he became England's first outfield player from outside the top-flight since Michael Gray in 1999.SUNDERLAND BBC Tyne & Wear sport Weather Official club website

Foxboro, Mass.-The New England Patriots announced that they have released veteran punter Lee Johnson today. Subsequently, the team signed defensive lineman David Nugent off their practice squad to remain at 53 players on the active roster.
Johnson, 39, was in his 17th NFL season, including his third with the Patriots. The 6-foot-2-inch, 202-pound punter was signed by the Patriots as a free agent on Feb. 18, 1999. He played in 37 games and totaled 203 punts for 8,578 yards (42.3 avg.) for the Patriots in just over two years. His 42.3-yard average per punt ranks fifth in franchise history. In 17 seasons, Johnson has accumulated 1,187 career punts for 50,473 yards. Both represent NFL career punting records. He had 305 punts downed inside the 20 and 137 career touchbacks. He also had a career long 76-yard punt in the season opener at Cincinnati (9/9/01).

# Patriots release Lee Johnson, sign David Nugent off Practice Squad
## Foxboro, Mass.-The New England Patriots announced that they have released veteran punter Lee Johnson today. Subsequently, the team signed defensive lineman David Nugent off their practice squad to remain at 53 players on the active roster.
Nugent, 23, was originally drafted by the Patriots in the sixth round (201st overall) of the 2000 NFL draft out of Purdue. The 6-foot-4-inch, 295-pound defensive end appeared in six games as a rookie and was credited with one defensive tackle. He was waived by the Patriots on Sept. 2, 2001, but was re-signed to the practice squad on Sept. 4.

**David James Nugent** (born 2 May 1985) is an English footballer who plays as a striker for Southern League Premier Division Central club [Anstey Nomads](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anstey_Nomads_F.C. "Anstey Nomads F.C.").

He started his career in 2002 when he signed his first professional contract with [Bury](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bury_F.C. "Bury F.C."). He left the club in 2005, when he joined [Preston North End](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Preston_North_End_F.C. "Preston North End F.C.") for two seasons. Nugent joined [Portsmouth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portsmouth_F.C. "Portsmouth F.C.") in 2007, and later joined [Burnley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burnley_F.C. "Burnley F.C.") for the 2009–10 season, before returning to Portsmouth for one final season in 2010. He signed for [Leicester City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leicester_City_F.C. "Leicester City F.C.") in 2011, where he played for the club for four seasons, before joining [Middlesbrough](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Middlesbrough_F.C. "Middlesbrough F.C.") in 2015. After helping Middlesbrough secure promotion to the Premier League, Nugent joined Derby County after his starting position at Middlesbrough was put in jeopardy. Nugent signed for [Tranmere Rovers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tranmere_Rovers_F.C. "Tranmere Rovers F.C.") on loan from [Preston North End](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Preston_North_End_F.C. "Preston North End F.C.") for the remainder of the 2020–21 season.
Nugent played for England at under-21 level, before playing one match and scoring for the senior team.

Born in Huyton, Merseyside, Nugent was a member of the [Liverpool](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liverpool_F.C. "Liverpool F.C.") youth academy but left aged 15.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Nugent#cite_note-4) It was only once he changed his position that he then became a professional with [Bury](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bury_F.C. "Bury F.C."), joining the club's successful Youth and Centre of Excellence department.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Nugent#cite_note-5) After making his debut as a substitute against [Port Vale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Port_Vale_F.C. "Port Vale F.C.") in March 2002 at the age of just 16, Nugent initially struggled to live up to his early potential, but an explosive start to the 2004–05 League Two season saw several larger clubs take an interest.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Nugent#cite_note-:0-6)
Although a target for rivals [Burnley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burnley_F.C. "Burnley F.C."), Nugent opted to join [Preston North End](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Preston_North_End_F.C. "Preston North End F.C.") rather than [Northampton Town](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Northampton_Town_F.C. "Northampton Town F.C.") from Bury in January 2005 for a fee of £100,000.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Nugent#cite_note-:0-6)

He scored 10 league goals in 32 Championship appearances in 2005–06, as Preston finished fourth, losing to [Leeds United](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leeds_United_F.C. "Leeds United F.C.") in the playoff semi-final, thus failing to gain promotion.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Nugent#cite_note-7) Despite transfer speculation, Nugent spent the following season at Preston, scoring 15 goals in 43 appearances, and winning England recognition.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Nugent#cite_note-:1-8) Preston finished seventh in 2006–07.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Nugent#cite_note-9)

David Nugent was loaned from Portsmouth to Burnley on September 1, 2009. On February 1, 2021, Nugent joined League Two club Tranmere Rovers, wearing the number 28 shirt and playing as a forward.
2
On January 1, 2005, Nugent transferred from Bury to Preston North End. On July 1, 2007, he transferred from Preston North End to Portsmouth. During his time at Portsmouth, then-manager Harry Redknapp considered selling Nugent to raise funds for the signing of Jermain Defoe.
8

In 2015, while playing for Leicester City in the Premier League, Nugent was active, contributing with goals or assists in matches against teams such as West Bromwich Albion and Tottenham Hotspur. On August 14, 2015, he transferred from Leicester City to Middlesbrough.
9
On January 9, 2017, Nugent transferred from Middlesbrough to Derby County. On December 23, 2017, in a Championship match where Derby County defeated Millwall 3-0, Nugent scored twice and provided an assist, helping his team achieve four consecutive victories.

## 1.outline


## 2.club career
Nugent, who was born in Highton, had an eye for soccer from a young age, to the point where he was praised for his excellent footwork at the tender age of three.[[2]](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%EB%8D%B0%EC%9D%B4%EB%B9%84%EB%93%9C%20%EB%89%B4%EC%A0%A0%ED%8A%B8#fn-2) He also said that he had been a fan of Everton since he was young .
He played for the local team St. Aloysius and **joined the Liverpool Academy,****Everton****'s****biggest****rival,** at the age of 7.[[3]](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%EB%8D%B0%EC%9D%B4%EB%B9%84%EB%93%9C%20%EB%89%B4%EC%A0%A0%ED%8A%B8#fn-3) He played as a winger . However, in 2000, when he was 14 years old, he was released from the Liverpool Academy.[[4]](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%EB%8D%B0%EC%9D%B4%EB%B9%84%EB%93%9C%20%EB%89%B4%EC%A0%A0%ED%8A%B8#fn-4)
Nugent, who returned to the local football team, scored a hat-trick in an 11-a-side tournament match, and thanks to this, Sheffield United , Sheffield Wednesday , Crewe , and Barry reportedly got the opportunity to try out.
He chose Berry and immediately joined the Berry youth team after scoring a hat-trick as a striker in the tryout match against Chesterfield .

## 2.club career
### 2.1.Berry FC
![Image 9](blob:http://localhost/36296cbfc2e6817583f0ac9e4a8a1c21)
He made his professional debut in the 2001-02 season, coming on as a substitute in the 84th minute of the second half in the 41st round match against Port Vale at the age of just 16. After relegation was virtually confirmed, he played the full 90 minutes in the final match against Peterborough .
He spent the 2002-03 and 2003-04 seasons mainly with the youth team.
In the 2004-05 season, Nugent returned to the first team and established himself as a starting striker at the age of 19, delivering an incredible performance by recording 11 goals and 3 assists in the first half alone. Naturally, this attracted the attention of higher-level clubs such as Burnley , Northampton , and Preston .

## 2.club career
### 2.2.Preston North End FC (1st generation)
![Image 11](blob:http://localhost/6151f349b614909b3ce71b9423f32029)  
**132 games, 38 goals, 9 assists**[[5]](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%EB%8D%B0%EC%9D%B4%EB%B9%84%EB%93%9C%20%EB%89%B4%EC%A0%A0%ED%8A%B8#fn-5)
During the winter transfer window of the 2004-05 season, Newgent finally negotiated with Preston , who was one of the leading candidates for promotion to the Premier League , and the transfer was completed for a fee of £100,000.
![Image 13](blob:http://localhost/79d70ef975ee55fcb9940319c9993614)
Nugent, who made his Preston debut in the 24th round of the league against Leicester City , quickly integrated into the team and recorded 8 goals and 1 assist, leading the team to the playoffs . Although Preston ultimately lost in the final and suffered the bitter disappointment of failing to gain promotion, Nugent's performance was enough to immediately attract the interest of Premier League clubs.
![Image 15](blob:http://localhost/744102acdbaa91c53c5f285ee1de50ea)  
**Football League Young Player of the Year**
In the 2005-06 season, he played in a total of 38 games and scored 11 goals, even winning the Football League Young Player of the Year award, but the team was eliminated in the playoff semifinals once again.
![Image 17](blob:http://localhost/d07dd210ea2e7624a9f66382ff11d4bf)  
**The monumental season that brought Nugent to fame**

## 2.club career
### 2.2.Preston North End FC (1st generation)
As a result, transfer rumors involving several clubs spread, but Nugent remained at Preston and set a new career high in the 2006-07 season with 17 goals and 8 assists in 48 matches. Thanks to this performance, **he had the honor of being selected for****the England national team****despite playing in the Championship, the second tier of** English football. However, Preston suffered a shocking two consecutive defeats at the end of the season, causing their ranking to plummet in an instant and preventing them from even advancing to the playoffs.
Eventually, Premier League clubs Sunderland and Portsmouth each offered a transfer fee of about £6 million, and Preston club also came to accept it.

## 2.club career
### 2.3.Portsmouth FC
On July 11, 2007, his move to Portsmouth was confirmed. The transfer fee was £6 million and the contract duration was four years.
He scored a goal in a League Cup match immediately after joining, but manager Harry Redknapp revealed that he planned to sell Nugent immediately if necessary to raise funds for the transfer market. In fact, he received interest from Derby County , but Nugent insisted on staying at Portsmouth.
However, during the 2007-08 season, he was relegated to a role primarily for cup competitions due to competition from numerous high-profile signings and his inability to integrate into the team's tactics. He was even scheduled to be loaned to Ipswich around March 2008, towards the end of the season , but suffered the humiliation of failing his medical test. The only consolation was that he managed to add an FA Cup victory to his career.
Although the team began to experience turmoil in the 2008-09 season, the attack was already filled with outstanding players such as Jermain Defoe and Peter Crouch , and Nugent himself was sidelined by injuries and unable to play in many matches. Nevertheless, he scored his Premier League debut goal against Redknapp's Tottenham , who had signed him but did not utilize him much, and secured a starting position by scoring consecutive goals against Fulham and Liverpool in the two matches surrounding that, which was at least a satisfactory achievement.
Entering the 2009-10 season, as Portsmouth's financial situation deteriorated further and players began leaving, he had an opportunity to step up as a starter. However, he suffered the ordeal of having his salary cut by two weeks and being kicked off the tour after getting into an argument with Mark Wilson during the preseason tour, and he remained a bench player even after the season opened.

## 2.club career
### 2.3.Portsmouth FC
#### 2.3.1.Burnley FC (loan)
Under these circumstances, on the last day of the transfer window, Premier League club Burnley expressed interest in Nugent, and on September 1, 2009, just before the transfer window closed, they signed a six-month loan with an option for a permanent transfer.
![Image 19](blob:http://localhost/3a3f476d67cad39a12eceb2d446a52fd)
After making his debut against Liverpool following his transfer to Burnley , he came on as a second-half substitute in the next match against Sunderland and delivered a fantastic performance by scoring multiple goals. Nugent became a semi-regular starter for Burnley.
However, a major setback occurred when the actual manager, Owen Coyle , left the team mid-season. First, his loan contract was extended until the end of the season. Under new manager Bryan Ross, he played as a starter, covering not only the striker position but also the winger role, yet he could not prevent Burnley's relegation. Furthermore, his parent club, Portsmouth , was in the worst possible situation, compounded by financial problems on top of relegation.

## 2.club career
### 2.3.Portsmouth FC
#### 2.3.2.after returning to lease
Ultimately, not only did he fail to attract the interest of other Premier League teams, but his permanent transfer to Burnley also fell through, leaving him with no choice but to return to Portsmouth . Return to the Championship after four seasons .
![Image 21](blob:http://localhost/c35a347d3f2b4b8cd2f4e66fd2d347ff)
After returning, he began the 2010-11 season as a left winger , the position he had played during his youth . Although he suffered from a severe goal drought after the season started, he scored his first goals with one assist in the 8th round of the league match against Leicester City . Subsequently, he recorded a total of 14 goals and 7 assists for the season, becoming the team's top scorer. It was the season in which he finally earned his keep since joining Portsmouth.
He ended his time at Portsmouth after his contract expired following the end of the season.

## 2.club career
### 2.4.Leicester City FC
![Image 23](blob:http://localhost/796d620cbe857b871c7a3dd2b5a5d281)  
**180 games, 59 goals, 28 assists**

## 2.club career
### 2.4.Leicester City FC
#### 2.4.1.2011-12 season
![Image 25](blob:http://localhost/b0691bc022c82fae28421123fabae82a)
It seemed as though the situation at Burnley would repeat itself after manager Eriksson, who had requested his signing in his first season, was sacked. However, under the guidance of Nigel Pearson, who had returned to the helm at Leicester City , Nugent established himself as a starter, recording a total of 16 goals and 8 assists that season, and even led Leicester City to a surprise quarter-final appearance in the FA Cup. Becoming the team's top scorer was an added bonus. Yet, despite being considered a title contender, the team finished the season in 9th place.

In the 2004-05 season, Nugent returned to the first team and established himself as a starting striker at the age of 19, delivering an incredible performance by recording 11 goals and 3 assists in the first half alone. Naturally, this attracted the attention of higher-level clubs such as Burnley , Northampton , and Preston .

### 2.2.Preston North End FC (1st generation)

## 2.club career
### 2.2.Preston North End FC (1st generation)
As a result, transfer rumors involving several clubs spread, but Nugent remained at Preston and set a new career high in the 2006-07 season with 17 goals and 8 assists in 48 matches. Thanks to this performance, **he had the honor of being selected for****the England national team****despite playing in the Championship, the second tier of** English football. However, Preston suffered a shocking two consecutive defeats at the end of the season, causing their ranking to plummet in an instant and preventing them from even advancing to the playoffs.
Eventually, Premier League clubs Sunderland and Portsmouth each offered a transfer fee of about £6 million, and Preston club also came to accept it.
texts.7:
## 2.club career
### 2.3.Portsmouth FC
On July 11, 2007, his move to Portsmouth was confirmed. The transfer fee was £6 million and the contract duration was four years.
He scored a goal in a League Cup match immediately after joining, but manager Harry Redknapp revealed that he planned to sell Nugent immediately if necessary to raise funds for the transfer market. In fact, he received interest from Derby County , but Nugent insisted on staying at Portsmouth.
However, during the 2007-08 season, he was relegated to a role primarily for cup competitions due to competition from numerous high-profile signings and his inability to integrate into the team's tactics. He was even scheduled to be loaned to Ipswich around March 2008, towards the end of the season , but suffered the humiliation of failing his medical test. The only consolation was that he managed to add an FA Cup victory to his career.
Although the team began to experience turmoil in the 2008-09 season, the attack was already filled with outstanding players such as Jermain Defoe and Peter Crouch , and Nugent himself was sidelined by injuries and unable to play in many matches. Nevertheless, he scored his Premier League debut goal against Redknapp's Tottenham , who had signed him but did not utilize him much, and secured a starting position by scoring consecutive goals against Fulham and Liverpool in the two matches surrounding that, which was at least a satisfactory achievement.
Entering the 2009-10 season, as Portsmouth's financial situation deteriorated further and players began leaving, he had an opportunity to step up as a starter. However, he suffered the ordeal of having his salary cut by two weeks and being kicked off the tour after getting into an argument with Mark Wilson during the preseason tour, and he remained a bench player even after the season opened.

## 2.club career
### 2.3.Portsmouth FC
#### 2.3.1.Burnley FC (loan)
Under these circumstances, on the last day of the transfer window, Premier League club Burnley expressed interest in Nugent, and on September 1, 2009, just before the transfer window closed, they signed a six-month loan with an option for a permanent transfer.
![Image 19](blob:http://localhost/3a3f476d67cad39a12eceb2d446a52fd)
After making his debut against Liverpool following his transfer to Burnley , he came on as a second-half substitute in the next match against Sunderland and delivered a fantastic performance by scoring multiple goals. Nugent became a semi-regular starter for Burnley.
However, a major setback occurred when the actual manager, Owen Coyle , left the team mid-season. First, his loan contract was extended until the end of the season. Under new manager Bryan Ross, he played as a starter, covering not only the striker position but also the winger role, yet he could not prevent Burnley's relegation. Furthermore, his parent club, Portsmouth , was in the worst possible situation, compounded by financial problems on top of relegation.

#### 2.3.2.after returning to lease
Ultimately, not only did he fail to attract the interest of other Premier League teams, but his permanent transfer to Burnley also fell through, leaving him with no choice but to return to Portsmouth . Return to the Championship after four seasons .
![Image 21](blob:http://localhost/c35a347d3f2b4b8cd2f4e66fd2d347ff)
After returning, he began the 2010-11 season as a left winger , the position he had played during his youth . Although he suffered from a severe goal drought after the season started, he scored his first goals with one assist in the 8th round of the league match against Leicester City . Subsequently, he recorded a total of 14 goals and 7 assists for the season, becoming the team's top scorer. It was the season in which he finally earned his keep since joining Portsmouth.
He ended his time at Portsmouth after his contract expired following the end of the season.

# Detroit Catholic Central High School
## Michael Nugent '81
*   Class 1981  
*   Induction 2022  
*   Sport(s)Cross Country
Michael Nugent was a four-year two sport athlete at Catholic Central (CC). He ran Cross Country from 1977 through 1980 and Track from 1978 to 1981. In the 1979 and 1980 cross country seasons Mike, as captain, led the Shamrocks to second place finishes in the Catholic League Championship meets. In the 1981 Michigan High School Athletic Association (MHSAA) Class A Track Championship meet, Mike placed third in the 3200-meter run with a time of 9:27.1 earning All-State Honors. He is third on the CC all-time 5K list at 15:46. Coach Magni said, “Mike was an unselfish hard working team leader who always wanted the team to do well.” Mike is grateful to Coach Tony Magni who encouraged him as a 9th grader to join the cross country and track programs. Mike Nugent, a four-year letter winner and honor roll student, was selected by his classmates as the 1981 Whalen Award Winner.
Mike moved onto Hillsdale College where he excelled. He lettered all four years in cross country, indoor track, and outdoor track and in Mike’s junior and senior years he was chosen Hillsdale’s team captain. He earned individual All American Honors both seasons by becoming the National Champion in the Indoor 3-mile run in 1984 (14:08.45) and 1985 (13:58.81) at the National Association of Intercollegiate Athletics (NAIA) National Championship meets. In the 1985 outdoor season he earned All-American and Academic All-American honors. He capped of his running career at Hillsdale by being chosen for the top Senior Man Award at Hillsdale which recognizes high academic and athletic achievement. In 2007 Mike Nugent was inducted into the Hillsdale Track and Field Hall of Fame.

# Detroit Catholic Central High School
## Michael Nugent '81
Mike earned his BA in English and Spanish from Hillsdale College, his MA in English from Wayne State University, and a Certificate of International School Leadership from the Principals Training Center. Mike has been in education since 1988 and joined the American School of Madrid’s (ASM) staff in 1995 as a Middle and High School English teacher. He was named the Middle School Director in 2011.
Michael Nugent is one of four brothers who graduated from CC: Tom ’78, Jim ’79 and Pat ’87. Mike and his wife, Esther, who is also in education, have two children, Sofia, and David. Both are attending university in Spain.
We know Mike lives the spirit of “Goodness Discipline and Knowledge” and are proud to induct him into the CC Athletic Hall of Fame.

# BBC SPORT | Football | Internationals | McClaren calls up striker Nugent
Nugent scored against Burnley on Saturday **Preston striker David Nugent has been called up for England's forthcoming Euro 2008 qualifiers as a replacement for the injured Darren Bent.** Aston Villa left back Gareth Barry has also been drafted into the squad. If he plays Nugent would be England's first outfield player from outside the top flight since Michael Gray in 1999. Nugent has scored 16 goals this season and is the first Preston player to be called up by England since Sir Tom Finney in 1959. **Interview: England boss Steve McClaren** **Interview: England's goalkeeping coach Ray Clemence** Nugent was playing for Bury in League Two only two years ago, but England coach Steve McClaren believes the player's form for the Under-21 team will enable him to cope with international football. "Internationally you look at the under-21s and if he can score at that level, and he has done," said McClaren. Full back Barry had been left out of the original party but earned a reprieve after Manchester United's Gary Neville was ruled out because of an ankle injury. McClaren's other defensive injury worry is Micah Richards' ongoing calf problem. Liverpool defender Jamie Carragher and Everton's Phil Neville will also be competing for the left-back slot. 606: DEBATE **Is Nugent ready for England?** Paul Fletcher - BBC Sport Barry received his first call-up for nearly four years when England played Spain in a friendly in February and played for most of the second half. However, despite Ashley Cole's suspension for the game against Israel and an injury to fellow left-back Wayne Bridge, the 26-year-old was initially dropped for the games against Israel and Andorra. The decision was criticised by Villa boss Martin O'Neill. Richards will join up with the squad on Tuesday and is calf problem will be assessed. Old Trafford captain Neville picked up an ankle injury against Bolton on Saturday and is set to be sidelined for three weeks. There was good news for England coach McClaren when Steven Gerrard was given the all-clear, despite limping out of the draw at Aston Villa. However, the England boss could lose other players to injury after Monday's FA Cup ties, with Manchester United facing Middlesbrough and Tottenham taking on Chelsea.

# Detroit Catholic Central High School
## Michael Nugent '81
*   Class 1981  
*   Induction 2022  
*   Sport(s)Cross Country
Michael Nugent was a four-year two sport athlete at Catholic Central (CC). He ran Cross Country from 1977 through 1980 and Track from 1978 to 1981. In the 1979 and 1980 cross country seasons Mike, as captain, led the Shamrocks to second place finishes in the Catholic League Championship meets. In the 1981 Michigan High School Athletic Association (MHSAA) Class A Track Championship meet, Mike placed third in the 3200-meter run with a time of 9:27.1 earning All-State Honors. He is third on the CC all-time 5K list at 15:46. Coach Magni said, “Mike was an unselfish hard working team leader who always wanted the team to do well.” Mike is grateful to Coach Tony Magni who encouraged him as a 9th grader to join the cross country and track programs. Mike Nugent, a four-year letter winner and honor roll student, was selected by his classmates as the 1981 Whalen Award Winner.
Mike moved onto Hillsdale College where he excelled. He lettered all four years in cross country, indoor track, and outdoor track and in Mike’s junior and senior years he was chosen Hillsdale’s team captain. He earned individual All American Honors both seasons by becoming the National Champion in the Indoor 3-mile run in 1984 (14:08.45) and 1985 (13:58.81) at the National Association of Intercollegiate Athletics (NAIA) National Championship meets. In the 1985 outdoor season he earned All-American and Academic All-American honors. He capped of his running career at Hillsdale by being chosen for the top Senior Man Award at Hillsdale which recognizes high academic and athletic achievement. In 2007 Mike Nugent was inducted into the Hillsdale Track and Field Hall of Fame.
texts.5:
# Detroit Catholic Central High School
## Michael Nugent '81
Mike earned his BA in English and Spanish from Hillsdale College, his MA in English from Wayne State University, and a Certificate of International School Leadership from the Principals Training Center. Mike has been in education since 1988 and joined the American School of Madrid’s (ASM) staff in 1995 as a Middle and High School English teacher. He was named the Middle School Director in 2011.
Michael Nugent is one of four brothers who graduated from CC: Tom ’78, Jim ’79 and Pat ’87. Mike and his wife, Esther, who is also in education, have two children, Sofia, and David. Both are attending university in Spain.
We know Mike lives the spirit of “Goodness Discipline and Knowledge” and are proud to induct him into the CC Athletic Hall of Fame.

# BBC SPORT | Football | Internationals | McClaren calls up striker Nugent
Nugent scored against Burnley on Saturday **Preston striker David Nugent has been called up for England's forthcoming Euro 2008 qualifiers as a replacement for the injured Darren Bent.** Aston Villa left back Gareth Barry has also been drafted into the squad. If he plays Nugent would be England's first outfield player from outside the top flight since Michael Gray in 1999. Nugent has scored 16 goals this season and is the first Preston player to be called up by England since Sir Tom Finney in 1959. **Interview: England boss Steve McClaren** **Interview: England's goalkeeping coach Ray Clemence** Nugent was playing for Bury in League Two only two years ago, but England coach Steve McClaren believes the player's form for the Under-21 team will enable him to cope with international football. "Internationally you look at the under-21s and if he can score at that level, and he has done," said McClaren. Full back Barry had been left out of the original party but earned a reprieve after Manchester United's Gary Neville was ruled out because of an ankle injury. McClaren's other defensive injury worry is Micah Richards' ongoing calf problem. Liverpool defender Jamie Carragher and Everton's Phil Neville will also be competing for the left-back slot. 606: DEBATE **Is Nugent ready for England?** Paul Fletcher - BBC Sport Barry received his first call-up for nearly four years when England played Spain in a friendly in February and played for most of the second half. However, despite Ashley Cole's suspension for the game against Israel and an injury to fellow left-back Wayne Bridge, the 26-year-old was initially dropped for the games against Israel and Andorra. The decision was criticised by Villa boss Martin O'Neill. Richards will join up with the squad on Tuesday and is calf problem will be assessed. Old Trafford captain Neville picked up an ankle injury against Bolton on Saturday and is set to be sidelined for three weeks. There was good news for England coach McClaren when Steven Gerrard was given the all-clear, despite limping out of the draw at Aston Villa. However, the England boss could lose other players to injury after Monday's FA Cup ties, with Manchester United facing Middlesbrough and Tottenham taking on Chelsea.

# Detroit Catholic Central High School
## Michael Nugent '81
*   Class 1981  
*   Induction 2022  
*   Sport(s)Cross Country
Michael Nugent was a four-year two sport athlete at Catholic Central (CC). He ran Cross Country from 1977 through 1980 and Track from 1978 to 1981. In the 1979 and 1980 cross country seasons Mike, as captain, led the Shamrocks to second place finishes in the Catholic League Championship meets. In the 1981 Michigan High School Athletic Association (MHSAA) Class A Track Championship meet, Mike placed third in the 3200-meter run with a time of 9:27.1 earning All-State Honors. He is third on the CC all-time 5K list at 15:46. Coach Magni said, “Mike was an unselfish hard working team leader who always wanted the team to do well.” Mike is grateful to Coach Tony Magni who encouraged him as a 9th grader to join the cross country and track programs. Mike Nugent, a four-year letter winner and honor roll student, was selected by his classmates as the 1981 Whalen Award Winner.
Mike moved onto Hillsdale College where he excelled. He lettered all four years in cross country, indoor track, and outdoor track and in Mike’s junior and senior years he was chosen Hillsdale’s team captain. He earned individual All American Honors both seasons by becoming the National Champion in the Indoor 3-mile run in 1984 (14:08.45) and 1985 (13:58.81) at the National Association of Intercollegiate Athletics (NAIA) National Championship meets. In the 1985 outdoor season he earned All-American and Academic All-American honors. He capped of his running career at Hillsdale by being chosen for the top Senior Man Award at Hillsdale which recognizes high academic and athletic achievement. In 2007 Mike Nugent was inducted into the Hillsdale Track and Field Hall of Fame.

# Detroit Catholic Central High School
## Michael Nugent '81
Mike earned his BA in English and Spanish from Hillsdale College, his MA in English from Wayne State University, and a Certificate of International School Leadership from the Principals Training Center. Mike has been in education since 1988 and joined the American School of Madrid’s (ASM) staff in 1995 as a Middle and High School English teacher. He was named the Middle School Director in 2011.
Michael Nugent is one of four brothers who graduated from CC: Tom ’78, Jim ’79 and Pat ’87. Mike and his wife, Esther, who is also in education, have two children, Sofia, and David. Both are attending university in Spain.
We know Mike lives the spirit of “Goodness Discipline and Knowledge” and are proud to induct him into the CC Athletic Hall of Fame.

**David James Nugent** (born 2 May 1985) is an English footballer who plays as a striker for Southern League Premier Division Central club [Anstey Nomads](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anstey_Nomads_F.C. "Anstey Nomads F.C.").

He started his career in 2002 when he signed his first professional contract with [Bury](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bury_F.C. "Bury F.C."). He left the club in 2005, when he joined [Preston North End](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Preston_North_End_F.C. "Preston North End F.C.") for two seasons. Nugent joined [Portsmouth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portsmouth_F.C. "Portsmouth F.C.") in 2007, and later joined [Burnley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burnley_F.C. "Burnley F.C.") for the 2009–10 season, before returning to Portsmouth for one final season in 2010. He signed for [Leicester City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leicester_City_F.C. "Leicester City F.C.") in 2011, where he played for the club for four seasons, before joining [Middlesbrough](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Middlesbrough_F.C. "Middlesbrough F.C.") in 2015. After helping Middlesbrough secure promotion to the Premier League, Nugent joined Derby County after his starting position at Middlesbrough was put in jeopardy. Nugent signed for [Tranmere Rovers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tranmere_Rovers_F.C. "Tranmere Rovers F.C.") on loan from [Preston North End](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Preston_North_End_F.C. "Preston North End F.C.") for the remainder of the 2020–21 season.
Nugent played for England at under-21 level, before playing one match and scoring for the senior team.

Born in Huyton, Merseyside, Nugent was a member of the [Liverpool](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liverpool_F.C. "Liverpool F.C.") youth academy but left aged 15.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Nugent#cite_note-4) It was only once he changed his position that he then became a professional with [Bury](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bury_F.C. "Bury F.C."), joining the club's successful Youth and Centre of Excellence department.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Nugent#cite_note-5) After making his debut as a substitute against [Port Vale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Port_Vale_F.C. "Port Vale F.C.") in March 2002 at the age of just 16, Nugent initially struggled to live up to his early potential, but an explosive start to the 2004–05 League Two season saw several larger clubs take an interest.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Nugent#cite_note-:0-6)
Although a target for rivals [Burnley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burnley_F.C. "Burnley F.C."), Nugent opted to join [Preston North End](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Preston_North_End_F.C. "Preston North End F.C.") rather than [Northampton Town](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Northampton_Town_F.C. "Northampton Town F.C.") from Bury in January 2005 for a fee of £100,000.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Nugent#cite_note-:0-6)

He scored 10 league goals in 32 Championship appearances in 2005–06, as Preston finished fourth, losing to [Leeds United](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leeds_United_F.C. "Leeds United F.C.") in the playoff semi-final, thus failing to gain promotion.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Nugent#cite_note-7) Despite transfer speculation, Nugent spent the following season at Preston, scoring 15 goals in 43 appearances, and winning England recognition.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Nugent#cite_note-:1-8) Preston finished seventh in 2006–07.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Nugent#cite_note-9)

# Ex-England striker David Nugent comes out of retirement aged 40 to sign for eighth-tier club
## **Former England star comes out of retirement to become player-coach of eighth-tier club**
Leicester came from three goals down to draw the friendly 3-3 and ultimately claim the win on penalties.
A shootout also proved to be the Nomads' undoing in the first round of the FA Trophy in October, having lost to Basford United.
Nugent will now hope to inspire their promotion push in the eighth tier, with his new team just three points from the playoff places.
The ex-England international played a key role in Leicester’s 2014 promotion and their Premier League survival the following season.
Since retiring, he has juggled sporadic media work covering his former club with his family duties.
4
Nugent has done media work for Leicester City TV since retiring Credit: Getty

# Ex-England striker David Nugent comes out of retirement aged 40 to sign for eighth-tier club
## David Nugent England goal
The ex-striker started his nomadic career at Bury after an unsuccessful stint in Liverpool's youth academy.
He went on to enjoy stints at Portsmouth, Burnley, Middlesbrough, Derby County, but remains most associated with Leicester.
Nugent spent four years at the King Power Stadium, scoring 59 goals and registering 28 assists in 180 appearances until his exit in 2015.
He famously remains one of England's all-time one-cap wonders, with his solitary cap in a Euro 2008 qualifier against Andorra.
4
Nugent rewarded McClaren's faith by scoring on his only Three Lions appearance Credit: Getty
He was handed a surprise call-up in 2007 by Steve McClaren, with the forward in fine form for Championship side Preston at the time.
Nugent became the first outfield player to feature for England while playing in the second tier since Sunderland icon Michael Gray in 1999.
The striker infamously scored on his only international appearance after prodding Jermain Defoe's goal-bound shot over the line from a yard out.

# Ex-England striker David Nugent comes out of retirement aged 40 to sign for eighth-tier club
## **Former England star comes out of retirement to become player-coach of eighth-tier club**
Leicester came from three goals down to draw the friendly 3-3 and ultimately claim the win on penalties.
A shootout also proved to be the Nomads' undoing in the first round of the FA Trophy in October, having lost to Basford United.
Nugent will now hope to inspire their promotion push in the eighth tier, with his new team just three points from the playoff places.
The ex-England international played a key role in Leicester’s 2014 promotion and their Premier League survival the following season.
Since retiring, he has juggled sporadic media work covering his former club with his family duties.
4
Nugent has done media work for Leicester City TV since retiring Credit: Getty
texts.12:
# Ex-England striker David Nugent comes out of retirement aged 40 to sign for eighth-tier club
## David Nugent England goal
The ex-striker started his nomadic career at Bury after an unsuccessful stint in Liverpool's youth academy.
He went on to enjoy stints at Portsmouth, Burnley, Middlesbrough, Derby County, but remains most associated with Leicester.
Nugent spent four years at the King Power Stadium, scoring 59 goals and registering 28 assists in 180 appearances until his exit in 2015.
He famously remains one of England's all-time one-cap wonders, with his solitary cap in a Euro 2008 qualifier against Andorra.
4
Nugent rewarded McClaren's faith by scoring on his only Three Lions appearance Credit: Getty
He was handed a surprise call-up in 2007 by Steve McClaren, with the forward in fine form for Championship side Preston at the time.
Nugent became the first outfield player to feature for England while playing in the second tier since Sunderland icon Michael Gray in 1999.
The striker infamously scored on his only international appearance after prodding Jermain Defoe's goal-bound shot over the line from a yard out.

**David James Nugent** (born 2 May 1985) is an English footballer who plays as a striker for Southern League Premier Division Central club [Anstey Nomads](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anstey_Nomads_F.C. "Anstey Nomads F.C.").

Nugent joined [Portsmouth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portsmouth_F.C. "Portsmouth F.C.") in 2007, and later joined [Burnley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burnley_F.C. "Burnley F.C.") for the 2009–10 season, before returning to Portsmouth for one final season in 2010. He signed for [Leicester City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leicester_City_F.C. "Leicester City F.C.") in 2011, where he played for the club for four seasons, before joining [Middlesbrough](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Middlesbrough_F.C. "Middlesbrough F.C.") in 2015. After helping Middlesbrough secure promotion to the Premier League, Nugent joined Derby County after his starting position at Middlesbrough was put in jeopardy. Nugent signed for [Tranmere Rovers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tranmere_Rovers_F.C. "Tranmere Rovers F.C.") on loan from [Preston North End](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Preston_North_End_F.C. ## **Former England star comes out of retirement to become player-coach of eighth-tier club**
Leicester came from three goals down to draw the friendly 3-3 and ultimately claim the win on penalties.
A shootout also proved to be the Nomads' undoing in the first round of the FA Trophy in October, having lost to Basford United.
Nugent will now hope to inspire their promotion push in the eighth tier, with his new team just three points from the playoff places.
The ex-England international played a key role in Leicester’s 2014 promotion and their Premier League survival the following season.
Since retiring, he has juggled sporadic media work covering his former club with his family duties.
4
Nugent has done media work for Leicester City TV since retiring Credit: Getty

# Ex-England striker David Nugent comes out of retirement aged 40 to sign for eighth-tier club
## David Nugent England goal
The ex-striker started his nomadic career at Bury after an unsuccessful stint in Liverpool's youth academy.
He went on to enjoy stints at Portsmouth, Burnley, Middlesbrough, Derby County, but remains most associated with Leicester.
Nugent spent four years at the King Power Stadium, scoring 59 goals and registering 28 assists in 180 appearances until his exit in 2015.
He famously remains one of England's all-time one-cap wonders, with his solitary cap in a Euro 2008 qualifier against Andorra.
4
Nugent rewarded McClaren's faith by scoring on his only Three Lions appearance Credit: Getty
He was handed a surprise call-up in 2007 by Steve McClaren, with the forward in fine form for Championship side Preston at the time.
Nugent became the first outfield player to feature for England while playing in the second tier since Sunderland icon Michael Gray in 1999.
The striker infamously scored on his only international appearance after prodding Jermain Defoe's goal-bound shot over the line from a yard out.

**Kevin Patrick Nugent** (born 10 April 1969) is an English professional football manager and former player. He is the manager of the [Millwall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Millwall_F.C. "Millwall F.C.") U23 team.

Nugent began his career at [Leyton Orient](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leyton_Orient_F.C. "Leyton Orient F.C.") in the 1980s and made over 100 appearances in all competitions for the club, spending time on loan at [Cork City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cork_City_F.C. "Cork City F.C.") during the 1988–89 season.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_Nugent_(footballer)#cite_note-2) After finishing the 1991–92 season as the club's top scorer, he signed for [Plymouth Argyle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plymouth_Argyle_F.C. "Plymouth Argyle F.C.") in March 1992 for a transfer fee of £200,000 and made over 100 appearances for Plymouth. In September 1995, he moved to [Bristol City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bristol_City_F.C. "Bristol City F.C.") for a fee of £75,000, although first-team opportunities were more limited.
Nugent signed for [Cardiff City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardiff_City_F.C. "Cardiff City F.C.") in June 1997 for a transfer fee of £65,000. After an injury hit first year at Ninian Park, Nugent enjoyed a strong second year, being awarded the club's player of the year award. He also later captained the side before an Achilles injury saw him lose his place in the side and later leave on a free transfer in January 2002 to return to Leyton Orient,[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_Nugent_(footballer)#cite_note-3) where his career had begun.
In January 2003, Nugent signed for [Swansea City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swansea_City_A.F.C. "Swansea City A.F.C.") on loan, making the move permanent a month later. He was released by the club's new manager Kenny Jackett in June 2004 but a week later, he was surprisingly re-signed as a player and also appointed assistant manager.

Including his appearances on loan, to the end of the 2005–06 season, Nugent had played 83 games for Swansea City in all competitions and had scored 19 goals. He retained his player registration, allowing him to play during injury crises, although he played only once during the 2005–06 season.
Kevin is an ex-pupil of Saint Ignatius College, Enfield.
Nugent started his coaching career as assistant manager to Kenny Jackett at Swansea City. When Jackett was sacked on 15 February 2007, Nugent became caretaker manager for two matches earning just one point. With Roberto Martínez taking over, and wanting to bring his own men in, Nugent's future was unclear until Martinez offered him the position of chief scout.
In June 2007, Nugent returned to his playing roots and became the Leyton Orient youth team manager. When Orient manager Martin Ling and his assistant Dean Smith were sacked on 18 January 2009, Nugent took over as caretaker manager. In his four games in charge, he won once; a shock victory at promotion chasing [Milton Keynes Dons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Milton_Keynes_Dons_F.C. "Milton Keynes Dons F.C."). Soon after Geraint Williams was installed as Leyton Orient's new manager, with Nugent retaining his role as assistant manager. On 3 April 2010, Williams was sacked and Nugent was once again installed as caretaker manager,[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_Nugent_(footballer)#cite_note-Leyton_Orient_part_company_with_Geraint_Williams_after_Hartlepool_loss-4) remaining in charge for a 2–1 defeat to [Southampton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southampton_F.C.

**Kevin Patrick Nugent** (born 10 April 1969) is an English professional football manager and former player. He is the manager of the [Millwall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Millwall_F.C. "Millwall F.C.") U23 team.
texts.3:
Nugent began his career at [Leyton Orient](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leyton_Orient_F.C. "Leyton Orient F.C.") in the 1980s and made over 100 appearances in all competitions for the club, spending time on loan at [Cork City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cork_City_F.C. "Cork City F.C.") during the 1988–89 season.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_Nugent_(footballer)#cite_note-2) After finishing the 1991–92 season as the club's top scorer, he signed for [Plymouth Argyle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plymouth_Argyle_F.C. "Plymouth Argyle F.C.") in March 1992 for a transfer fee of £200,000 and made over 100 appearances for Plymouth. In September 1995, he moved to [Bristol City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bristol_City_F.C. "Bristol City F.C.") for a fee of £75,000, although first-team opportunities were more limited.
Nugent signed for [Cardiff City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardiff_City_F.C. "Cardiff City F.C.") in June 1997 for a transfer fee of £65,000. After an injury hit first year at Ninian Park, Nugent enjoyed a strong second year, being awarded the club's player of the year award. He also later captained the side before an Achilles injury saw him lose his place in the side and later leave on a free transfer in January 2002 to return to Leyton Orient,[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_Nugent_(footballer)#cite_note-3) where his career had begun.
In January 2003, Nugent signed for [Swansea City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swansea_City_A.F.C. "Swansea City A.F.C.") on loan, making the move permanent a month later. He was released by the club's new manager Kenny Jackett in June 2004 but a week later, he was surprisingly re-signed as a player and also appointed assistant manager.
texts.4:
Including his appearances on loan, to the end of the 2005–06 season, Nugent had played 83 games for Swansea City in all competitions and had scored 19 goals. He retained his player registration, allowing him to play during injury crises, although he played only once during the 2005–06 season.
Kevin is an ex-pupil of Saint Ignatius College, Enfield.
Nugent started his coaching career as assistant manager to Kenny Jackett at Swansea City. When Jackett was sacked on 15 February 2007, Nugent became caretaker manager for two matches earning just one point. With Roberto Martínez taking over, and wanting to bring his own men in, Nugent's future was unclear until Martinez offered him the position of chief scout.
In June 2007, Nugent returned to his playing roots and became the Leyton Orient youth team manager. When Orient manager Martin Ling and his assistant Dean Smith were sacked on 18 January 2009, Nugent took over as caretaker manager. In his four games in charge, he won once; a shock victory at promotion chasing [Milton Keynes Dons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Milton_Keynes_Dons_F.C. "Milton Keynes Dons F.C."). Soon after Geraint Williams was installed as Leyton Orient's new manager, with Nugent retaining his role as assistant manager. On 3 April 2010, Williams was sacked and Nugent was once again installed as caretaker manager,[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_Nugent_(footballer)#cite_note-Leyton_Orient_part_company_with_Geraint_Williams_after_Hartlepool_loss-4) remaining in charge for a 2–1 defeat to [Southampton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southampton_F.C.

"Leyton Orient F.C.") in the 1980s and made over 100 appearances in all competitions for the club, spending time on loan at [Cork City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cork_City_F.C. "Cork City F.C.") during the 1988–89 season.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_Nugent_(footballer)#cite_note-2) After finishing the 1991–92 season as the club's top scorer, he signed for [Plymouth Argyle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plymouth_Argyle_F.C. "Plymouth Argyle F.C.") in March 1992 for a transfer fee of £200,000 and made over 100 appearances for Plymouth. In September 1995, he moved to [Bristol City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bristol_City_F.C. "Bristol City F.C.") for a fee of £75,000, although first-team opportunities were more limited.
Nugent signed for [Cardiff City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardiff_City_F.C. "Cardiff City F.C.") in June 1997 for a transfer fee of £65,000. After an injury hit first year at Ninian Park, Nugent enjoyed a strong second year, being awarded the club's player of the year award. He also later captained the side before an Achilles injury saw him lose his place in the side and later leave on a free transfer in January 2002 to return to Leyton Orient,[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_Nugent_(footballer)#cite_note-3) where his career had begun.
In January 2003, Nugent signed for [Swansea City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swansea_City_A.F.C. "Swansea City A.F.C.") on loan, making the move permanent a month later. He was released by the club's new manager Kenny Jackett in June 2004 but a week later, he was surprisingly re-signed as a player and also appointed assistant manager.

Including his appearances on loan, to the end of the 2005–06 season, Nugent had played 83 games for Swansea City in all competitions and had scored 19 goals. He retained his player registration, allowing him to play during injury crises, although he played only once during the 2005–06 season.
Kevin is an ex-pupil of Saint Ignatius College, Enfield.
Nugent started his coaching career as assistant manager to Kenny Jackett at Swansea City. When Jackett was sacked on 15 February 2007, Nugent became caretaker manager for two matches earning just one point. With Roberto Martínez taking over, and wanting to bring his own men in, Nugent's future was unclear until Martinez offered him the position of chief scout.
In June 2007, Nugent returned to his playing roots and became the Leyton Orient youth team manager. When Orient manager Martin Ling and his assistant Dean Smith were sacked on 18 January 2009, Nugent took over as caretaker manager. In his four games in charge, he won once; a shock victory at promotion chasing [Milton Keynes Dons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Milton_Keynes_Dons_F.C. "Milton Keynes Dons F.C."). Soon after Geraint Williams was installed as Leyton Orient's new manager, with Nugent retaining his role as assistant manager. On 3 April 2010, Williams was sacked and Nugent was once again installed as caretaker manager,[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_Nugent_(footballer)#cite_note-Leyton_Orient_part_company_with_Geraint_Williams_after_Hartlepool_loss-4) remaining in charge for a 2–1 defeat to [Southampton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southampton_F.C.

# Ex-England striker David Nugent comes out of retirement aged 40 to sign for eighth-tier club
## **Former England star comes out of retirement to become player-coach of eighth-tier club**
Leicester came from three goals down to draw the friendly 3-3 and ultimately claim the win on penalties.
A shootout also proved to be the Nomads' undoing in the first round of the FA Trophy in October, having lost to Basford United.
Nugent will now hope to inspire their promotion push in the eighth tier, with his new team just three points from the playoff places.
The ex-England international played a key role in Leicester’s 2014 promotion and their Premier League survival the following season.
Since retiring, he has juggled sporadic media work covering his former club with his family duties.
4
Nugent has done media work for Leicester City TV since retiring Credit: Getty

# Ex-England striker David Nugent comes out of retirement aged 40 to sign for eighth-tier club
## David Nugent England goal
The ex-striker started his nomadic career at Bury after an unsuccessful stint in Liverpool's youth academy.
He went on to enjoy stints at Portsmouth, Burnley, Middlesbrough, Derby County, but remains most associated with Leicester.
Nugent spent four years at the King Power Stadium, scoring 59 goals and registering 28 assists in 180 appearances until his exit in 2015.
He famously remains one of England's all-time one-cap wonders, with his solitary cap in a Euro 2008 qualifier against Andorra.
4
Nugent rewarded McClaren's faith by scoring on his only Three Lions appearance Credit: Getty
He was handed a surprise call-up in 2007 by Steve McClaren, with the forward in fine form for Championship side Preston at the time.
Nugent became the first outfield player to feature for England while playing in the second tier since Sunderland icon Michael Gray in 1999.
The striker infamously scored on his only international appearance after prodding Jermain Defoe's goal-bound shot over the line from a yard out.

**Kevin Patrick Nugent** (born 10 April 1969) is an English professional football manager and former player. He is the manager of the [Millwall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Millwall_F.C. "Millwall F.C.") U23 team.

Nugent began his career at [Leyton Orient](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leyton_Orient_F.C. "Leyton Orient F.C.") in the 1980s and made over 100 appearances in all competitions for the club, spending time on loan at [Cork City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cork_City_F.C. "Cork City F.C.") during the 1988–89 season.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_Nugent_(footballer)#cite_note-2) After finishing the 1991–92 season as the club's top scorer, he signed for [Plymouth Argyle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plymouth_Argyle_F.C. "Plymouth Argyle F.C.") in March 1992 for a transfer fee of £200,000 and made over 100 appearances for Plymouth. In September 1995, he moved to [Bristol City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bristol_City_F.C. "Bristol City F.C.") for a fee of £75,000, although first-team opportunities were more limited.
Nugent signed for [Cardiff City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardiff_City_F.C. "Cardiff City F.C.") in June 1997 for a transfer fee of £65,000. After an injury hit first year at Ninian Park, Nugent enjoyed a strong second year, being awarded the club's player of the year award. He also later captained the side before an Achilles injury saw him lose his place in the side and later leave on a free transfer in January 2002 to return to Leyton Orient,[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_Nugent_(footballer)#cite_note-3) where his career had begun.
In January 2003, Nugent signed for [Swansea City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swansea_City_A.F.C. "Swansea City A.F.C.") on loan, making the move permanent a month later. He was released by the club's new manager Kenny Jackett in June 2004 but a week later, he was surprisingly re-signed as a player and also appointed assistant manager.

Including his appearances on loan, to the end of the 2005–06 season, Nugent had played 83 games for Swansea City in all competitions and had scored 19 goals. He retained his player registration, allowing him to play during injury crises, although he played only once during the 2005–06 season.
Kevin is an ex-pupil of Saint Ignatius College, Enfield.
Nugent started his coaching career as assistant manager to Kenny Jackett at Swansea City. When Jackett was sacked on 15 February 2007, Nugent became caretaker manager for two matches earning just one point. With Roberto Martínez taking over, and wanting to bring his own men in, Nugent's future was unclear until Martinez offered him the position of chief scout.
In June 2007, Nugent returned to his playing roots and became the Leyton Orient youth team manager. When Orient manager Martin Ling and his assistant Dean Smith were sacked on 18 January 2009, Nugent took over as caretaker manager. In his four games in charge, he won once; a shock victory at promotion chasing [Milton Keynes Dons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Milton_Keynes_Dons_F.C. "Milton Keynes Dons F.C."). Soon after Geraint Williams was installed as Leyton Orient's new manager, with Nugent retaining his role as assistant manager. On 3 April 2010, Williams was sacked and Nugent was once again installed as caretaker manager,[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_Nugent_(footballer)#cite_note-Leyton_Orient_part_company_with_Geraint_Williams_after_Hartlepool_loss-4) remaining in charge for a 2–1 defeat to [Southampton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southampton_F.C.

### Exeter City 0 Cardiff City 2.
Match Report by **Ted Davenport**
Saturday 20 March 1999.
EXETER's play-off pretensions were exposed cruelly as they lost to a table topping side for the second time in two weeks.Fox's side matched Cardiff in most areas but the clinical finishing of former Plymouth striker Kevin Nugent was the difference between the sides.Exeter created a heap of chances but rarely looked like putting them away, while Cardiff showed they are at the top of the pile with two superbly taken goals from Nugent either side of the break.Fox shocked fans by leaving top scorer Steve Flack on the bench and starting the game with loan signings Brian Quailey and Peter Tosh as his strike duo.The move prompted suspicions that the 15-goal for- ward could be on the move before next Thursday's transfer deadline although officially his absence was attributed to lack of form and goals in recent games.Veterans Darran Rowbotham and Jon Gittens were both suspended and club skipper Jon Richardson was still injured so former Cardiff player Lee Baddeley played in the heart of defence with Chris Curran. Geoff Breslan returned to join Jason Rees, Chris Holloway and Jimmy Gardner in midfield.Exeter dominated the first half but went in a goal down thanks to one lapse of concentration in defence.Rising midfield star Geoff Breslan came within inches of giving the home side the perfect start on three minutes after an exquisite pass from Paul Tosh but his first time drive flew just inches past the post. Within three minutes Tosh himself had a great chance. He found space from a Shaun Gale corner but his volley soared well over the bar. The on-loan Scottish striker had another shot blocked by a defender before Exeter were gifted a golden chance by referee Barry Knight after a Cardiff defender was penalised for having a foot up as he tackled Lee Baddeley inside the penalty area.The referee awarded an indirect free kick instead of a penalty and then moved the Cardiff wall back almost to the goal line. Graeme Power's fierce shot rebounded off a defender to Brian Quailey but his effort blocked.At this stage Exeter were shading a tight but scrappy game in which neither side could find room or time to put together any coherent movement.Right back Shaun Gale and Quailey both tried long range shots which went closer to the corner flag than the goal while a Chris Holloway's effort from inside the area flew well wide.

### Exeter City 0 Cardiff City 2.
Cardiff turned the game upside down in the 30th minute when Nugent put the table-toppers ahead.The Bluebirds had barely threatened before midfielder Mark Bonner launched his soaring cross from the right wing which found Jason Bowen's head.He nodded down towards goal and Baddeley looked favourite to clear until Nugent dived in to slam it past the stranded Ashley Bayes. The goal inspired Cardiff who were unlucky not to go. two up in first half injury time when Graham Mitchell's pass dissected the Exeter defence and let in Bowen whose clever chip slipped just past the post with Bayes beaten.Nugent made the game safe for Cardiff 13 minutes into the second half when he scored against the run of play with a brave diving header as he leapt between Lee Baddeley and Chris Curran to leave Bayes no chance as he met Danny Hill's left wing cross.The goal came just moments after Exeter had their best chances of the game with a sustained at- tack in which Tosh and Quailey both had goal- bound shots blocked before the ball fell to Quailey who bobbled the ball wide of the open net.The incident followed 10 minutes of sustained pres- sure in which Quailey and Tosh both had chances but put them either straight at keeper Jon Hallworth or wide of the target.Exeter looked sharper after Steve Flack came off the bench on 55 minutes, but their finishing still let them down as Flack's effort from a right wing cross went straight to the keeper and Tosh's header did not have enough power to beat Nugent's goal line clearance.Exeter continued to press without posing a real threat and their best chance came when Chris Curran's close range shot. was brilliantly saved on 65 minutes and Flack's volley went into the side netting just moments later. The keeper had to be sharp again to deny Tosh's header from a long Curran throw and the striker put another effort wide three minutes before the end. At the other end Cardiff looked lethal on the break as substitute John Williams twice ran clear of his former Exeter team-mates but could not beat Ashley Bayes.
**Exeter City**Bayes Gale Power Baddeley Curran Breslan Quailey Rees Tosh Holloway Gardner Substitutes: Flack (for Breslan, 54 mins) Wilkinson (for Quailey, 72), Blake (not used).
**Cardiff City:**

Cardiff - Nugent 39, 60.

Leicester came from three goals down to draw the friendly 3-3 and ultimately claim the win on penalties.
A shootout also proved to be the Nomads' undoing in the first round of the FA Trophy in October, having lost to Basford United.
Nugent will now hope to inspire their promotion push in the eighth tier, with his new team just three points from the playoff places.
The ex-England international played a key role in Leicester’s 2014 promotion and their Premier League survival the following season.
Since retiring, he has juggled sporadic media work covering his former club with his family duties.

# Ex-England striker David Nugent comes out of retirement aged 40 to sign for eighth-tier club
## David Nugent England goal
The ex-striker started his nomadic career at Bury after an unsuccessful stint in Liverpool's youth academy.
He went on to enjoy stints at Portsmouth, Burnley, Middlesbrough, Derby County, but remains most associated with Leicester.
Nugent spent four years at the King Power Stadium, scoring 59 goals and registering 28 assists in 180 appearances until his exit in 2015.
He famously remains one of England's all-time one-cap wonders, with his solitary cap in a Euro 2008 qualifier against Andorra.
4
Nugent rewarded McClaren's faith by scoring on his only Three Lions appearance Credit: Getty
He was handed a surprise call-up in 2007 by Steve McClaren, with the forward in fine form for Championship side Preston at the time.
Nugent became the first outfield player to feature for England while playing in the second tier since Sunderland icon Michael Gray in 1999.
The striker infamously scored on his only international appearance after prodding Jermain Defoe's goal-bound shot over the line from a yard out.

### Exeter City 0 Cardiff City 2.
Match Report by **Ted Davenport**
Saturday 20 March 1999.
EXETER's play-off pretensions were exposed cruelly as they lost to a table topping side for the second time in two weeks.Fox's side matched Cardiff in most areas but the clinical finishing of former Plymouth striker Kevin Nugent was the difference between the sides.Exeter created a heap of chances but rarely looked like putting them away, while Cardiff showed they are at the top of the pile with two superbly taken goals from Nugent either side of the break.Fox shocked fans by leaving top scorer Steve Flack on the bench and starting the game with loan signings Brian Quailey and Peter Tosh as his strike duo.The move prompted suspicions that the 15-goal for- ward could be on the move before next Thursday's transfer deadline although officially his absence was attributed to lack of form and goals in recent games.Veterans Darran Rowbotham and Jon Gittens were both suspended and club skipper Jon Richardson was still injured so former Cardiff player Lee Baddeley played in the heart of defence with Chris Curran. Geoff Breslan returned to join Jason Rees, Chris Holloway and Jimmy Gardner in midfield.Exeter dominated the first half but went in a goal down thanks to one lapse of concentration in defence.Rising midfield star Geoff Breslan came within inches of giving the home side the perfect start on three minutes after an exquisite pass from Paul Tosh but his first time drive flew just inches past the post. Within three minutes Tosh himself had a great chance. He found space from a Shaun Gale corner but his volley soared well over the bar. The on-loan Scottish striker had another shot blocked by a defender before Exeter were gifted a golden chance by referee Barry Knight after a Cardiff defender was penalised for having a foot up as he tackled Lee Baddeley inside the penalty area.The referee awarded an indirect free kick instead of a penalty and then moved the Cardiff wall back almost to the goal line. Graeme Power's fierce shot rebounded off a defender to Brian Quailey but his effort blocked.At this stage Exeter were shading a tight but scrappy game in which neither side could find room or time to put together any coherent movement.Right back Shaun Gale and Quailey both tried long range shots which went closer to the corner flag than the goal while a Chris Holloway's effort from inside the area flew well wide.

### Exeter City 0 Cardiff City 2.
Cardiff turned the game upside down in the 30th minute when Nugent put the table-toppers ahead.The Bluebirds had barely threatened before midfielder Mark Bonner launched his soaring cross from the right wing which found Jason Bowen's head.He nodded down towards goal and Baddeley looked favourite to clear until Nugent dived in to slam it past the stranded Ashley Bayes. The goal inspired Cardiff who were unlucky not to go. two up in first half injury time when Graham Mitchell's pass dissected the Exeter defence and let in Bowen whose clever chip slipped just past the post with Bayes beaten.Nugent made the game safe for Cardiff 13 minutes into the second half when he scored against the run of play with a brave diving header as he leapt between Lee Baddeley and Chris Curran to leave Bayes no chance as he met Danny Hill's left wing cross.The goal came just moments after Exeter had their best chances of the game with a sustained at- tack in which Tosh and Quailey both had goal- bound shots blocked before the ball fell to Quailey who bobbled the ball wide of the open net.The incident followed 10 minutes of sustained pres- sure in which Quailey and Tosh both had chances but put them either straight at keeper Jon Hallworth or wide of the target.Exeter looked sharper after Steve Flack came off the bench on 55 minutes, but their finishing still let them down as Flack's effort from a right wing cross went straight to the keeper and Tosh's header did not have enough power to beat Nugent's goal line clearance.Exeter continued to press without posing a real threat and their best chance came when Chris Curran's close range shot. was brilliantly saved on 65 minutes and Flack's volley went into the side netting just moments later. The keeper had to be sharp again to deny Tosh's header from a long Curran throw and the striker put another effort wide three minutes before the end. At the other end Cardiff looked lethal on the break as substitute John Williams twice ran clear of his former Exeter team-mates but could not beat Ashley Bayes.

**Kevin Patrick Nugent** (born 10 April 1969) is an English professional football manager and former player. He is the manager of the [Millwall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Millwall_F.C. "Millwall F.C.") U23 team.

Nugent began his career at [Leyton Orient](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leyton_Orient_F.C. "Leyton Orient F.C.") in the 1980s and made over 100 appearances in all competitions for the club, spending time on loan at [Cork City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cork_City_F.C. "Cork City F.C.") during the 1988–89 season.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_Nugent_(footballer)#cite_note-2) After finishing the 1991–92 season as the club's top scorer, he signed for [Plymouth Argyle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plymouth_Argyle_F.C. "Plymouth Argyle F.C.") in March 1992 for a transfer fee of £200,000 and made over 100 appearances for Plymouth. In September 1995, he moved to [Bristol City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bristol_City_F.C. "Bristol City F.C.") for a fee of £75,000, although first-team opportunities were more limited.
Nugent signed for [Cardiff City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardiff_City_F.C. "Cardiff City F.C.") in June 1997 for a transfer fee of £65,000. After an injury hit first year at Ninian Park, Nugent enjoyed a strong second year, being awarded the club's player of the year award. He also later captained the side before an Achilles injury saw him lose his place in the side and later leave on a free transfer in January 2002 to return to Leyton Orient,[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_Nugent_(footballer)#cite_note-3) where his career had begun.
In January 2003, Nugent signed for [Swansea City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swansea_City_A.F.C. "Swansea City A.F.C.") on loan, making the move permanent a month later. He was released by the club's new manager Kenny Jackett in June 2004 but a week later, he was surprisingly re-signed as a player and also appointed assistant manager.

Including his appearances on loan, to the end of the 2005–06 season, Nugent had played 83 games for Swansea City in all competitions and had scored 19 goals. He retained his player registration, allowing him to play during injury crises, although he played only once during the 2005–06 season.
Kevin is an ex-pupil of Saint Ignatius College, Enfield.
Nugent started his coaching career as assistant manager to Kenny Jackett at Swansea City. When Jackett was sacked on 15 February 2007, Nugent became caretaker manager for two matches earning just one point. With Roberto Martínez taking over, and wanting to bring his own men in, Nugent's future was unclear until Martinez offered him the position of chief scout.
In June 2007, Nugent returned to his playing roots and became the Leyton Orient youth team manager. When Orient manager Martin Ling and his assistant Dean Smith were sacked on 18 January 2009, Nugent took over as caretaker manager. In his four games in charge, he won once; a shock victory at promotion chasing [Milton Keynes Dons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Milton_Keynes_Dons_F.C. "Milton Keynes Dons F.C."). Soon after Geraint Williams was installed as Leyton Orient's new manager, with Nugent retaining his role as assistant manager. On 3 April 2010, Williams was sacked and Nugent was once again installed as caretaker manager,[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_Nugent_(footballer)#cite_note-Leyton_Orient_part_company_with_Geraint_Williams_after_Hartlepool_loss-4) remaining in charge for a 2–1 defeat to [Southampton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southampton_F.C.

# Ex-England striker David Nugent comes out of retirement aged 40 to sign for eighth-tier club
## David Nugent England goal
The ex-striker started his nomadic career at Bury after an unsuccessful stint in Liverpool's youth academy.
He went on to enjoy stints at Portsmouth, Burnley, Middlesbrough, Derby County, but remains most associated with Leicester.
Nugent spent four years at the King Power Stadium, scoring 59 goals and registering 28 assists in 180 appearances until his exit in 2015.
He famously remains one of England's all-time one-cap wonders, with his solitary cap in a Euro 2008 qualifier against Andorra.

He was handed a surprise call-up in 2007 by Steve McClaren, with the forward in fine form for Championship side Preston at the time.
Nugent became the first outfield player to feature for England while playing in the second tier since Sunderland icon Michael Gray in 1999.
The striker infamously scored on his only international appearance after prodding Jermain Defoe's goal-bound shot over the line from a yard out.
