**David James Nugent** (born 2 May 1985) is an English footballer who plays as a striker for Southern League Premier Division Central club [Anstey Nomads](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anstey_Nomads_F.C. "Anstey Nomads F.C.").

He started his career in 2002 when he signed his first professional contract with [Bury](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bury_F.C. "Bury F.C."). He left the club in 2005, when he joined [Preston North End](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Preston_North_End_F.C. "Preston North End F.C.") for two seasons. Nugent joined [Portsmouth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portsmouth_F.C. "Portsmouth F.C.") in 2007, and later joined [Burnley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burnley_F.C. "Burnley F.C.") for the 2009–10 season, before returning to Portsmouth for one final season in 2010. He signed for [Leicester City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leicester_City_F.C. "Leicester City F.C.") in 2011, where he played for the club for four seasons, before joining [Middlesbrough](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Middlesbrough_F.C. "Middlesbrough F.C.") in 2015. After helping Middlesbrough secure promotion to the Premier League, Nugent joined Derby County after his starting position at Middlesbrough was put in jeopardy. Nugent signed for [Tranmere Rovers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tranmere_Rovers_F.C. "Tranmere Rovers F.C.") on loan from [Preston North End](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Preston_North_End_F.C. "Preston North End F.C.") for the remainder of the 2020–21 season.
Nugent played for England at under-21 level, before playing one match and scoring for the senior team.

Born in Huyton, Merseyside, Nugent was a member of the [Liverpool](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liverpool_F.C. "Liverpool F.C.") youth academy but left aged 15.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Nugent#cite_note-4) It was only once he changed his position that he then became a professional with [Bury](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bury_F.C. "Bury F.C."), joining the club's successful Youth and Centre of Excellence department.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Nugent#cite_note-5) After making his debut as a substitute against [Port Vale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Port_Vale_F.C. "Port Vale F.C.") in March 2002 at the age of just 16, Nugent initially struggled to live up to his early potential, but an explosive start to the 2004–05 League Two season saw several larger clubs take an interest.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Nugent#cite_note-:0-6)
Although a target for rivals [Burnley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burnley_F.C. "Burnley F.C."), Nugent opted to join [Preston North End](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Preston_North_End_F.C. "Preston North End F.C.") rather than [Northampton Town](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Northampton_Town_F.C. "Northampton Town F.C.") from Bury in January 2005 for a fee of £100,000.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Nugent#cite_note-:0-6)

He scored 10 league goals in 32 Championship appearances in 2005–06, as Preston finished fourth, losing to [Leeds United](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leeds_United_F.C. "Leeds United F.C.") in the playoff semi-final, thus failing to gain promotion.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Nugent#cite_note-7) Despite transfer speculation, Nugent spent the following season at Preston, scoring 15 goals in 43 appearances, and winning England recognition.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Nugent#cite_note-:1-8) Preston finished seventh in 2006–07.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Nugent#cite_note-9)

# Detroit Catholic Central High School
## Michael Nugent '81
*   Class 1981  
*   Induction 2022  
*   Sport(s)Cross Country
Michael Nugent was a four-year two sport athlete at Catholic Central (CC). He ran Cross Country from 1977 through 1980 and Track from 1978 to 1981. In the 1979 and 1980 cross country seasons Mike, as captain, led the Shamrocks to second place finishes in the Catholic League Championship meets. In the 1981 Michigan High School Athletic Association (MHSAA) Class A Track Championship meet, Mike placed third in the 3200-meter run with a time of 9:27.1 earning All-State Honors. He is third on the CC all-time 5K list at 15:46. Coach Magni said, “Mike was an unselfish hard working team leader who always wanted the team to do well.” Mike is grateful to Coach Tony Magni who encouraged him as a 9th grader to join the cross country and track programs. Mike Nugent, a four-year letter winner and honor roll student, was selected by his classmates as the 1981 Whalen Award Winner.
Mike moved onto Hillsdale College where he excelled. He lettered all four years in cross country, indoor track, and outdoor track and in Mike’s junior and senior years he was chosen Hillsdale’s team captain. He earned individual All American Honors both seasons by becoming the National Champion in the Indoor 3-mile run in 1984 (14:08.45) and 1985 (13:58.81) at the National Association of Intercollegiate Athletics (NAIA) National Championship meets. In the 1985 outdoor season he earned All-American and Academic All-American honors. He capped of his running career at Hillsdale by being chosen for the top Senior Man Award at Hillsdale which recognizes high academic and athletic achievement. In 2007 Mike Nugent was inducted into the Hillsdale Track and Field Hall of Fame.

# Detroit Catholic Central High School
## Michael Nugent '81
Mike earned his BA in English and Spanish from Hillsdale College, his MA in English from Wayne State University, and a Certificate of International School Leadership from the Principals Training Center. Mike has been in education since 1988 and joined the American School of Madrid’s (ASM) staff in 1995 as a Middle and High School English teacher. He was named the Middle School Director in 2011.
Michael Nugent is one of four brothers who graduated from CC: Tom ’78, Jim ’79 and Pat ’87. Mike and his wife, Esther, who is also in education, have two children, Sofia, and David. Both are attending university in Spain.
We know Mike lives the spirit of “Goodness Discipline and Knowledge” and are proud to induct him into the CC Athletic Hall of Fame.

# Detroit Catholic Central High School
## Michael Nugent '81
*   Class 1981  
*   Induction 2022  
*   Sport(s)Cross Country
Michael Nugent was a four-year two sport athlete at Catholic Central (CC). He ran Cross Country from 1977 through 1980 and Track from 1978 to 1981. In the 1979 and 1980 cross country seasons Mike, as captain, led the Shamrocks to second place finishes in the Catholic League Championship meets. In the 1981 Michigan High School Athletic Association (MHSAA) Class A Track Championship meet, Mike placed third in the 3200-meter run with a time of 9:27.1 earning All-State Honors. He is third on the CC all-time 5K list at 15:46. Coach Magni said, “Mike was an unselfish hard working team leader who always wanted the team to do well.” Mike is grateful to Coach Tony Magni who encouraged him as a 9th grader to join the cross country and track programs. Mike Nugent, a four-year letter winner and honor roll student, was selected by his classmates as the 1981 Whalen Award Winner.
Mike moved onto Hillsdale College where he excelled. He lettered all four years in cross country, indoor track, and outdoor track and in Mike’s junior and senior years he was chosen Hillsdale’s team captain. He earned individual All American Honors both seasons by becoming the National Champion in the Indoor 3-mile run in 1984 (14:08.45) and 1985 (13:58.81) at the National Association of Intercollegiate Athletics (NAIA) National Championship meets. In the 1985 outdoor season he earned All-American and Academic All-American honors. He capped of his running career at Hillsdale by being chosen for the top Senior Man Award at Hillsdale which recognizes high academic and athletic achievement. In 2007 Mike Nugent was inducted into the Hillsdale Track and Field Hall of Fame.

# Detroit Catholic Central High School
## Michael Nugent '81
Mike earned his BA in English and Spanish from Hillsdale College, his MA in English from Wayne State University, and a Certificate of International School Leadership from the Principals Training Center. Mike has been in education since 1988 and joined the American School of Madrid’s (ASM) staff in 1995 as a Middle and High School English teacher. He was named the Middle School Director in 2011.
Michael Nugent is one of four brothers who graduated from CC: Tom ’78, Jim ’79 and Pat ’87. Mike and his wife, Esther, who is also in education, have two children, Sofia, and David. Both are attending university in Spain.
We know Mike lives the spirit of “Goodness Discipline and Knowledge” and are proud to induct him into the CC Athletic Hall of Fame.

**David James Nugent** (born 2 May 1985) is an English footballer who plays as a striker for Southern League Premier Division Central club [Anstey Nomads](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anstey_Nomads_F.C. "Anstey Nomads F.C.").
texts.3:
He started his career in 2002 when he signed his first professional contract with [Bury](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bury_F.C. "Bury F.C."). He left the club in 2005, when he joined [Preston North End](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Preston_North_End_F.C. "Preston North End F.C.") for two seasons. Nugent joined [Portsmouth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portsmouth_F.C. "Portsmouth F.C.") in 2007, and later joined [Burnley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burnley_F.C. "Burnley F.C.") for the 2009–10 season, before returning to Portsmouth for one final season in 2010. He signed for [Leicester City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leicester_City_F.C. "Leicester City F.C.") in 2011, where he played for the club for four seasons, before joining [Middlesbrough](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Middlesbrough_F.C. "Middlesbrough F.C.") in 2015. After helping Middlesbrough secure promotion to the Premier League, Nugent joined Derby County after his starting position at Middlesbrough was put in jeopardy. Nugent signed for [Tranmere Rovers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tranmere_Rovers_F.C. "Tranmere Rovers F.C.") on loan from [Preston North End](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Preston_North_End_F.C. "Preston North End F.C.") for the remainder of the 2020–21 season.
Nugent played for England at under-21 level, before playing one match and scoring for the senior team.
texts.4:
Born in Huyton, Merseyside, Nugent was a member of the [Liverpool](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liverpool_F.C. "Liverpool F.C.") youth academy but left aged 15.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Nugent#cite_note-4) It was only once he changed his position that he then became a professional with [Bury](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bury_F.C. "Bury F.C."), joining the club's successful Youth and Centre of Excellence department.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Nugent#cite_note-5) After making his debut as a substitute against [Port Vale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Port_Vale_F.C. "Port Vale F.C.") in March 2002 at the age of just 16, Nugent initially struggled to live up to his early potential, but an explosive start to the 2004–05 League Two season saw several larger clubs take an interest.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Nugent#cite_note-:0-6)
Although a target for rivals [Burnley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burnley_F.C. "Burnley F.C."), Nugent opted to join [Preston North End](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Preston_North_End_F.C. "Preston North End F.C.") rather than [Northampton Town](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Northampton_Town_F.C. "Northampton Town F.C.") from Bury in January 2005 for a fee of £100,000.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Nugent#cite_note-:0-6)
texts.5: He scored 10 league goals in 32 Championship appearances in 2005–06, as Preston finished fourth, losing to [Leeds United](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leeds_United_F.C. "Leeds United F.C.") in the playoff semi-final, thus failing to gain promotion.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Nugent#cite_note-7) Despite transfer speculation, Nugent spent the following season at Preston, scoring 15 goals in 43 appearances, and winning England recognition.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Nugent#cite_note-:1-8) Preston finished seventh in 2006–07.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Nugent#cite_note-9)

# Detroit Catholic Central High School
## Michael Nugent '81
*   Class 1981  
*   Induction 2022  
*   Sport(s)Cross Country
Michael Nugent was a four-year two sport athlete at Catholic Central (CC). He ran Cross Country from 1977 through 1980 and Track from 1978 to 1981. In the 1979 and 1980 cross country seasons Mike, as captain, led the Shamrocks to second place finishes in the Catholic League Championship meets. In the 1981 Michigan High School Athletic Association (MHSAA) Class A Track Championship meet, Mike placed third in the 3200-meter run with a time of 9:27.1 earning All-State Honors. He is third on the CC all-time 5K list at 15:46. Coach Magni said, “Mike was an unselfish hard working team leader who always wanted the team to do well.” Mike is grateful to Coach Tony Magni who encouraged him as a 9th grader to join the cross country and track programs. Mike Nugent, a four-year letter winner and honor roll student, was selected by his classmates as the 1981 Whalen Award Winner.
Mike moved onto Hillsdale College where he excelled. He lettered all four years in cross country, indoor track, and outdoor track and in Mike’s junior and senior years he was chosen Hillsdale’s team captain. He earned individual All American Honors both seasons by becoming the National Champion in the Indoor 3-mile run in 1984 (14:08.45) and 1985 (13:58.81) at the National Association of Intercollegiate Athletics (NAIA) National Championship meets. In the 1985 outdoor season he earned All-American and Academic All-American honors. He capped of his running career at Hillsdale by being chosen for the top Senior Man Award at Hillsdale which recognizes high academic and athletic achievement. In 2007 Mike Nugent was inducted into the Hillsdale Track and Field Hall of Fame.

# Detroit Catholic Central High School
## Michael Nugent '81
Mike earned his BA in English and Spanish from Hillsdale College, his MA in English from Wayne State University, and a Certificate of International School Leadership from the Principals Training Center. Mike has been in education since 1988 and joined the American School of Madrid’s (ASM) staff in 1995 as a Middle and High School English teacher. He was named the Middle School Director in 2011.
Michael Nugent is one of four brothers who graduated from CC: Tom ’78, Jim ’79 and Pat ’87. Mike and his wife, Esther, who is also in education, have two children, Sofia, and David. Both are attending university in Spain.
We know Mike lives the spirit of “Goodness Discipline and Knowledge” and are proud to induct him into the CC Athletic Hall of Fame.

**David James Nugent** (born 2 May 1985) is an English footballer who plays as a striker for Southern League Premier Division Central club [Anstey Nomads](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anstey_Nomads_F.C. "Anstey Nomads F.C.").

He started his career in 2002 when he signed his first professional contract with [Bury](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bury_F.C. "Bury F.C."). He left the club in 2005, when he joined [Preston North End](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Preston_North_End_F.C. "Preston North End F.C.") for two seasons. Nugent joined [Portsmouth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portsmouth_F.C. "Portsmouth F.C.") in 2007, and later joined [Burnley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burnley_F.C. "Burnley F.C.") for the 2009–10 season, before returning to Portsmouth for one final season in 2010. He signed for [Leicester City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leicester_City_F.C. "Leicester City F.C.") in 2011, where he played for the club for four seasons, before joining [Middlesbrough](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Middlesbrough_F.C. "Middlesbrough F.C.") in 2015. After helping Middlesbrough secure promotion to the Premier League, Nugent joined Derby County after his starting position at Middlesbrough was put in jeopardy. Nugent signed for [Tranmere Rovers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tranmere_Rovers_F.C. "Tranmere Rovers F.C.") on loan from [Preston North End](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Preston_North_End_F.C. "Preston North End F.C.") for the remainder of the 2020–21 season.
Nugent played for England at under-21 level, before playing one match and scoring for the senior team.

Born in Huyton, Merseyside, Nugent was a member of the [Liverpool](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liverpool_F.C. "Liverpool F.C.") youth academy but left aged 15.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Nugent#cite_note-4) It was only once he changed his position that he then became a professional with [Bury](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bury_F.C. "Bury F.C."), joining the club's successful Youth and Centre of Excellence department.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Nugent#cite_note-5) After making his debut as a substitute against [Port Vale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Port_Vale_F.C. "Port Vale F.C.") in March 2002 at the age of just 16, Nugent initially struggled to live up to his early potential, but an explosive start to the 2004–05 League Two season saw several larger clubs take an interest.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Nugent#cite_note-:0-6)
Although a target for rivals [Burnley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burnley_F.C. "Burnley F.C."), Nugent opted to join [Preston North End](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Preston_North_End_F.C. "Preston North End F.C.") rather than [Northampton Town](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Northampton_Town_F.C. "Northampton Town F.C.") from Bury in January 2005 for a fee of £100,000.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Nugent#cite_note-:0-6)

He scored 10 league goals in 32 Championship appearances in 2005–06, as Preston finished fourth, losing to [Leeds United](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leeds_United_F.C. "Leeds United F.C.") in the playoff semi-final, thus failing to gain promotion.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Nugent#cite_note-7) Despite transfer speculation, Nugent spent the following season at Preston, scoring 15 goals in 43 appearances, and winning England recognition.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Nugent#cite_note-:1-8) Preston finished seventh in 2006–07.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Nugent#cite_note-9)

Born in Huyton, Merseyside, Nugent was a member of the [Liverpool](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liverpool_F.C. "Liverpool F.C.") youth academy but left aged 15.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Nugent#cite_note-4) It was only once he changed his position that he then became a professional with [Bury](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bury_F.C. "Bury F.C."), joining the club's successful Youth and Centre of Excellence department.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Nugent#cite_note-5) After making his debut as a substitute against [Port Vale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Port_Vale_F.C. "Port Vale F.C.") in March 2002 at the age of just 16, Nugent initially struggled to live up to his early potential, but an explosive start to the 2004–05 League Two season saw several larger clubs take an interest.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Nugent#cite_note-:0-6)
Although a target for rivals [Burnley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burnley_F.C. "Burnley F.C."), Nugent opted to join [Preston North End](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Preston_North_End_F.C. "Preston North End F.C.") rather than [Northampton Town](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Northampton_Town_F.C. "Northampton Town F.C.") from Bury in January 2005 for a fee of £100,000.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Nugent#cite_note-:0-6)

He scored 10 league goals in 32 Championship appearances in 2005–06, as Preston finished fourth, losing to [Leeds United](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leeds_United_F.C. "Leeds United F.C.") in the playoff semi-final, thus failing to gain promotion.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Nugent#cite_note-7) Despite transfer speculation, Nugent spent the following season at Preston, scoring 15 goals in 43 appearances, and winning England recognition.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Nugent#cite_note-:1-8) Preston finished seventh in 2006–07.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Nugent#cite_note-9)

# Ex-England striker David Nugent comes out of retirement aged 40 to sign for eighth-tier club
## **Former England star comes out of retirement to become player-coach of eighth-tier club**
Leicester came from three goals down to draw the friendly 3-3 and ultimately claim the win on penalties.
A shootout also proved to be the Nomads' undoing in the first round of the FA Trophy in October, having lost to Basford United.
Nugent will now hope to inspire their promotion push in the eighth tier, with his new team just three points from the playoff places.
The ex-England international played a key role in Leicester’s 2014 promotion and their Premier League survival the following season.
Since retiring, he has juggled sporadic media work covering his former club with his family duties.
4
Nugent has done media work for Leicester City TV since retiring Credit: Getty

# Ex-England striker David Nugent comes out of retirement aged 40 to sign for eighth-tier club
## David Nugent England goal
The ex-striker started his nomadic career at Bury after an unsuccessful stint in Liverpool's youth academy.
He went on to enjoy stints at Portsmouth, Burnley, Middlesbrough, Derby County, but remains most associated with Leicester.
Nugent spent four years at the King Power Stadium, scoring 59 goals and registering 28 assists in 180 appearances until his exit in 2015.
He famously remains one of England's all-time one-cap wonders, with his solitary cap in a Euro 2008 qualifier against Andorra.
4
Nugent rewarded McClaren's faith by scoring on his only Three Lions appearance Credit: Getty
He was handed a surprise call-up in 2007 by Steve McClaren, with the forward in fine form for Championship side Preston at the time.
Nugent became the first outfield player to feature for England while playing in the second tier since Sunderland icon Michael Gray in 1999.
The striker infamously scored on his only international appearance after prodding Jermain Defoe's goal-bound shot over the line from a yard out.

# BBC SPORT | Football | My Club | Preston | Sunderland withdraw Nugent offer
E-mail this to a friend Printable version Sunderland withdraw Nugent offer  Nugent joined Preston from Bury in January 2005 **Sunderland have pulled out of the race for Preston striker David Nugent.** According to the Black Cats website, they agreed a fee believed to be £7m with the North End for the 22-year-old but will now focus on other targets. Club chief executive Peter Walker said: "I can confirm we have withdrawn our offer for the player. "Naturally work continues behind the scenes to strengthen our squad ahead of the new season and talks are on-going with a number of targets." Nugent was given permission to speak to two clubs after he returned from duty with the England Under-21 squad at the European Championship last month. One of the teams was believed to be Sunderland, while West Ham and Everton were also linked with him. BBC Sport understands that talks had taken place with the player and his representatives for a month before Sunderland boss Roy Keane became frustrated with the situation. 606: DEBATE Your views on Nugent's future Nugent joined Preston from Bury in January 2005 for a fee believed to be in the region of £100,000. The Liverpool-born forward has made 94 Championship appearances for Preston, scoring 33 goals. Sheffield United tried to buy him in the January 2007 transfer window but North End rejected the offer. But the striker made it clear last season that he saw his future in the Premiership. "I want to be playing in the Premiership week in, week out, that's where I need to be," he said. "I want it to be with Preston, but if not, it'll have to be somewhere else." Preston finished seventh in last season's Championship, missing out on a place in the play-offs. Nugent is an Everton fan and has previously said: "My hero was Duncan Ferguson and, hopefully, I will play for them in my career and I'm confident I will do." He made his full England debut in the win over Andorra in March, scoring in the final minute of the game. The cap was the first by a Preston player since Sir Tom Finney and he became England's first outfield player from outside the top-flight since Michael Gray in 1999.SUNDERLAND BBC Tyne & Wear sport Weather Official club website

**David James Nugent** (born 2 May 1985) is an English footballer who plays as a striker for Southern League Premier Division Central club [Anstey Nomads](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anstey_Nomads_F.C. "Anstey Nomads F.C.").
texts.3:
He started his career in 2002 when he signed his first professional contract with [Bury](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bury_F.C. "Bury F.C."). He left the club in 2005, when he joined [Preston North End](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Preston_North_End_F.C. "Preston North End F.C.") for two seasons. Nugent joined [Portsmouth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portsmouth_F.C. "Portsmouth F.C.") in 2007, and later joined [Burnley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burnley_F.C. "Burnley F.C.") for the 2009–10 season, before returning to Portsmouth for one final season in 2010. He signed for [Leicester City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leicester_City_F.C. "Leicester City F.C.") in 2011, where he played for the club for four seasons, before joining [Middlesbrough](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Middlesbrough_F.C. "Middlesbrough F.C.") in 2015. After helping Middlesbrough secure promotion to the Premier League, Nugent joined Derby County after his starting position at Middlesbrough was put in jeopardy. Nugent signed for [Tranmere Rovers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tranmere_Rovers_F.C. "Tranmere Rovers F.C.") on loan from [Preston North End](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Preston_North_End_F.C. "Preston North End F.C.") for the remainder of the 2020–21 season.
Nugent played for England at under-21 level, before playing one match and scoring for the senior team.
texts.4:
Born in Huyton, Merseyside, Nugent was a member of the [Liverpool](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liverpool_F.C. "Liverpool F.C.") youth academy but left aged 15.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Nugent#cite_note-4) It was only once he changed his position that he then became a professional with [Bury](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bury_F.C. "Bury F.C."), joining the club's successful Youth and Centre of Excellence department.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Nugent#cite_note-5) After making his debut as a substitute against [Port Vale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Port_Vale_F.C. "Port Vale F.C.") in March 2002 at the age of just 16, Nugent initially struggled to live up to his early potential, but an explosive start to the 2004–05 League Two season saw several larger clubs take an interest.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Nugent#cite_note-:0-6)
Although a target for rivals [Burnley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burnley_F.C. "Burnley F.C."), Nugent opted to join [Preston North End](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Preston_North_End_F.C. "Preston North End F.C.") rather than [Northampton Town](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Northampton_Town_F.C. "Northampton Town F.C.") from Bury in January 2005 for a fee of £100,000.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Nugent#cite_note-:0-6)
texts.5: He scored 10 league goals in 32 Championship appearances in 2005–06, as Preston finished fourth, losing to [Leeds United](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leeds_United_F.C. "Leeds United F.C.") in the playoff semi-final, thus failing to gain promotion.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Nugent#cite_note-7) Despite transfer speculation, Nugent spent the following season at Preston, scoring 15 goals in 43 appearances, and winning England recognition.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Nugent#cite_note-:1-8) Preston finished seventh in 2006–07.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Nugent#cite_note-9)

## **Former England star comes out of retirement to become player-coach of eighth-tier club**
Leicester came from three goals down to draw the friendly 3-3 and ultimately claim the win on penalties.
A shootout also proved to be the Nomads' undoing in the first round of the FA Trophy in October, having lost to Basford United.
Nugent will now hope to inspire their promotion push in the eighth tier, with his new team just three points from the playoff places.
The ex-England international played a key role in Leicester’s 2014 promotion and their Premier League survival the following season.
Since retiring, he has juggled sporadic media work covering his former club with his family duties.

# Ex-England striker David Nugent comes out of retirement aged 40 to sign for eighth-tier club
## David Nugent England goal
The ex-striker started his nomadic career at Bury after an unsuccessful stint in Liverpool's youth academy.
He went on to enjoy stints at Portsmouth, Burnley, Middlesbrough, Derby County, but remains most associated with Leicester.
Nugent spent four years at the King Power Stadium, scoring 59 goals and registering 28 assists in 180 appearances until his exit in 2015.
He famously remains one of England's all-time one-cap wonders, with his solitary cap in a Euro 2008 qualifier against Andorra.
4
Nugent rewarded McClaren's faith by scoring on his only Three Lions appearance Credit: Getty
He was handed a surprise call-up in 2007 by Steve McClaren, with the forward in fine form for Championship side Preston at the time.
Nugent became the first outfield player to feature for England while playing in the second tier since Sunderland icon Michael Gray in 1999.
The striker infamously scored on his only international appearance after prodding Jermain Defoe's goal-bound shot over the line from a yard out.

# BBC SPORT | Football | My Club | Preston | Sunderland withdraw Nugent offer
E-mail this to a friend Printable version Sunderland withdraw Nugent offer  Nugent joined Preston from Bury in January 2005 **Sunderland have pulled out of the race for Preston striker David Nugent.** According to the Black Cats website, they agreed a fee believed to be £7m with the North End for the 22-year-old but will now focus on other targets. Club chief executive Peter Walker said: "I can confirm we have withdrawn our offer for the player. "Naturally work continues behind the scenes to strengthen our squad ahead of the new season and talks are on-going with a number of targets." Nugent was given permission to speak to two clubs after he returned from duty with the England Under-21 squad at the European Championship last month. One of the teams was believed to be Sunderland, while West Ham and Everton were also linked with him. BBC Sport understands that talks had taken place with the player and his representatives for a month before Sunderland boss Roy Keane became frustrated with the situation. 606: DEBATE Your views on Nugent's future Nugent joined Preston from Bury in January 2005 for a fee believed to be in the region of £100,000. The Liverpool-born forward has made 94 Championship appearances for Preston, scoring 33 goals. Sheffield United tried to buy him in the January 2007 transfer window but North End rejected the offer. But the striker made it clear last season that he saw his future in the Premiership. "I want to be playing in the Premiership week in, week out, that's where I need to be," he said. "I want it to be with Preston, but if not, it'll have to be somewhere else." Preston finished seventh in last season's Championship, missing out on a place in the play-offs. Nugent is an Everton fan and has previously said: "My hero was Duncan Ferguson and, hopefully, I will play for them in my career and I'm confident I will do." He made his full England debut in the win over Andorra in March, scoring in the final minute of the game. The cap was the first by a Preston player since Sir Tom Finney and he became England's first outfield player from outside the top-flight since Michael Gray in 1999.SUNDERLAND BBC Tyne & Wear sport Weather Official club website

**David James Nugent** (born 2 May 1985) is an English footballer who plays as a striker for Southern League Premier Division Central club [Anstey Nomads](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anstey_Nomads_F.C. "Anstey Nomads F.C.").

He started his career in 2002 when he signed his first professional contract with [Bury](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bury_F.C. "Bury F.C."). He left the club in 2005, when he joined [Preston North End](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Preston_North_End_F.C. "Preston North End F.C.") for two seasons. Nugent joined [Portsmouth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portsmouth_F.C. "Portsmouth F.C.") in 2007, and later joined [Burnley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burnley_F.C. "Burnley F.C.") for the 2009–10 season, before returning to Portsmouth for one final season in 2010. He signed for [Leicester City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leicester_City_F.C. "Leicester City F.C.") in 2011, where he played for the club for four seasons, before joining [Middlesbrough](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Middlesbrough_F.C. "Middlesbrough F.C.") in 2015. After helping Middlesbrough secure promotion to the Premier League, Nugent joined Derby County after his starting position at Middlesbrough was put in jeopardy. Nugent signed for [Tranmere Rovers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tranmere_Rovers_F.C. "Tranmere Rovers F.C.") on loan from [Preston North End](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Preston_North_End_F.C. "Preston North End F.C.") for the remainder of the 2020–21 season.
Nugent played for England at under-21 level, before playing one match and scoring for the senior team.

Born in Huyton, Merseyside, Nugent was a member of the [Liverpool](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liverpool_F.C. "Liverpool F.C.") youth academy but left aged 15.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Nugent#cite_note-4) It was only once he changed his position that he then became a professional with [Bury](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bury_F.C. "Bury F.C."), joining the club's successful Youth and Centre of Excellence department.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Nugent#cite_note-5) After making his debut as a substitute against [Port Vale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Port_Vale_F.C. "Port Vale F.C.") in March 2002 at the age of just 16, Nugent initially struggled to live up to his early potential, but an explosive start to the 2004–05 League Two season saw several larger clubs take an interest.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Nugent#cite_note-:0-6)
Although a target for rivals [Burnley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burnley_F.C. "Burnley F.C."), Nugent opted to join [Preston North End](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Preston_North_End_F.C.
